checks.name: no-hot-temporary-collection-control
checks.command: test -z "$(sed -n '/pub(crate) fn react_into/,/fn consume_path_outcome/p' truelearner/crates/body/src/core.rs | rg 'collect::<Vec|Vec::new|\.clone\(\)')"

checks.name: regression-suite
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path truelearner/Cargo.toml -p truelearner-body --lib --test engine --test attachment --test calibration --test physics --test behavior_contract

checks.name: performance-controls
checks.command: cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path truelearner/Cargo.toml -p truelearner-body --example engine_cost && cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path truelearner/Cargo.toml -p truelearner-body --example link_cost

findings: The internal reaction path now classifies each moment participant once and consumes compact MomentFact values in the three original edit phases.
Empty internal reactions bypass apply; non-empty edits and applied identity mappings reuse capacity inside Activity-owned ReactionScratch.
Ready paths, flat connected outcomes, world parents, and winner indexes are reused; per-world path clones and collected return vectors are gone from the internal wave path.
Return selection and retirement iterate Body::live_returns and do not scan all link memory.
The old black-box contract passed 3 of 3 tests, the compact-body contract passed 6 of 6 tests, and checkpoint passed 9 of 9 tests.
The known advanced body-law boundary remained exactly 17 passing and 11 failing tests, so no previously passing advanced law regressed.
The independent primitive-wave median was 40.01 ns versus 42.48 ns immediately before this change; active-link propagation measured 35.17 ns per link.
residual_uncertainty: The existing benchmarks cover primitive waves and linear active propagation, not allocation counts during a learning-heavy wave; benchmark deltas may also vary with host noise.
